findings.issue: Wrong reading of 一週間: it is read いっしゅうかん (with geminate っ), never いちしゅうかん.
findings.current: なつやすみまで、あといちしゅうかんです。
findings.suggested: なつやすみまで、あといっしゅうかんです。

findings.issue: In the compound 一週間 the numeral 一 is read いっ (isshuukan), not いち.
やつ means 'guy/fellow', not 'face' — looks like a back-translation of pt 'cara' via its wrong sense ('face'); '(he has)' compounds the error (JP has copula だ = 'he is').
findings.current: As for him, what a detestable face (he has)!
findings.suggested: As for him, what a detestable guy (he is)!

findings.issue: Carries the same reading error as kana: 'ichishuukan' should be 'isshuukan' (this is a wrong syllable, separate from the known punctuation issue).
'todavia' in modern pt-BR is only adversative ('however/no entanto') — a false friend of English temporal 'yet'. It never glosses temporal まだ ('still').
'He rarely fails to work' composes in English to 'he almost always works' — the opposite of めったに働かない. 'fails to' is not a mirror of ない; it inverts the sense.
findings.current: As for him, he rarely fails to work.
findings.suggested: As for him, he rarely works (lit.: rarely + works-not).

findings.issue: 'raramente não trabalha' composes in PT to 'quase sempre trabalha' — opposite meaning. The corpus device elsewhere (cf. 'vai-não' in sent:tatoeba-110869) hyphenates the negative to avoid this inversion.
findings.current: Quanto a ele, raramente não trabalha.

findings.issue: 'cleverly' misattributes skill to the victim; まんまと modifying the victim's verb かかった means 'completely / right into (the trap)', exactly as the token gloss says.
findings.current: He [topic] cleverly fell into / got caught in the trap.
findings.suggested: He [topic] fell right into / got neatly caught in the trap.

findings.issue: 'habilmente' (skillfully) misattributes skill to the victim; まんまと here is 'direitinho/completamente', matching the token gloss and the pt translation.
'primeiro' renders the wrong sense of まず: combined with a negative (まず〜ない) it means 'practically/certainly (not)', not 'first'.
findings.current: Ele-TÓPICO primeiro raramente barbeiro a vai-não.
findings.suggested: Ele-TÓPICO praticamente raramente barbeiro a vai-não.

findings.issue: 'fairly' here is the dated sense 'completely/utterly'; modern readers parse it as 'somewhat' or 'justly', obscuring まんまと for learners.
findings.current: He was fairly caught in the trap.
findings.suggested: He fell right into the trap.

findings.issue: The intensifier まったく (the very point highlighted in the explanation) is dropped in pt; en keeps it as 'quite'.
findings.suggested: Ele é totalmente jovem de espírito.

findings.issue: まず is omitted from the literal mirror, while lit_pt renders it ('primeiro') — the two literal fields should cover the same morphemes.
findings.current: As for him, he rarely goes to the barber.
findings.suggested: As for him, he practically never goes to the barber.

findings.issue: Literal field neither mirrors the JP order (cf. lit_pt) nor keeps the habitual non-past: 'I'll' reads as a one-off future, but 着きます here is habitual 'I arrive'; だいたい's approximation is kept but structure is lost.
findings.suggested: Approximately, at 8 o'clock, at home (I) arrive.

findings.issue: Misplaced parenthesis: it opens before 'the target くなかった' and swallows the final two sentences about the particle の; it should close right after くなかった.
findings.current: (the target くなかった. At the end, the final particle の gives an explanatory/soft tone, like someone justifying or telling something.)
findings.suggested: (the target くなかった). At the end, the final particle の gives an explanatory/soft tone, like someone justifying or telling something.

findings.issue: Same misplaced parenthesis as expl_en: it should close after くなかった instead of wrapping the last two sentences.
findings.current: (o foco-alvo くなかった. No fim, a partícula final の dá um tom explicativo/suave, como quem está justificando ou contando algo.)
findings.suggested: (o foco-alvo くなかった). No fim, a partícula final の dá um tom explicativo/suave, como quem está justificando ou contando algo.

findings.issue: The past-tense auxiliary だ (た voiced after 苦しん) is left with null gloss/role, unlike every other past auxiliary in the file (cf. かかっ+た labelled 'auxiliar de passado'); the 苦しん note even points to it.
